paragraphs: Posted by Lily. Last week, our school had a swimming event at the school pool. The pool is big, and it has clean blue water. Four classes took part, including Pat's class, Tom's class, my class, and Sam's class. Many parents came to watch, including Mom and Dad. The day was bright, and the pool was full of noise. Almost everyone wore a bright swimming cap. Mia took photos, and afterwards she made an album for the blog.

The rules were simple. The event began at nine o'clock, and each class had twenty minutes in the pool. After each class, the pool was empty for ten minutes, and Coach Matt checked the water. There were four lanes, and there were ten children per lane. Each child swam two laps, and Coach Matt counted every lap. He stood at the end of the pool with a loud whistle. He told us, "Nobody may run on the wet floor." We put our bags and shoes in a box near the door. Teacher Kim told us, "Every child must wear a cap."

The order was clear. Pat's class went first. Tom's class went second. My class went after Tom's class. Sam's class went last. While we waited, the Explorers sat on a bench and watched the other children. Leo made a poster that said, "Go, swimmers!" The children of Pat's class were small, and they clapped for each friend. Mia and I drank water and talked about the event.

After Tom's class left the pool, Mia looked at the clock on the wall. Then she put on her cap and smiled at me. Coach Matt called our class, and we walked to the water. I took a big breath. The water was cold at first, but it was nice after a minute. I swam two laps, and Mia swam in the next lane. May was not fast, but she did not stop. Leo swam two laps first, and then he held his poster over his head and shouted our names.

When I got out, Dad gave me a towel, and Mom took a photo. Mom said, "You swam well." May's mom and dad clapped for her too. Sam's class swam last, and then everybody went home. Do you like swimming? I like it because it is good exercise, and it is fun with friends.
